newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber retreats to close weak on lower cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber retreats to close weak on lower cash.

text.p: CME lumber futures remained under pressure from weak cash and finished mostly lower, despite early runups on short-covering and new speculative buying, traders said.
Lumber closed $2.40 per tbf higher to $4.00 lower with only January and March up. July ended $2.30 lower at $352.40 and September was off $2.10 at $346.50 per tbf.

Futures ran up for sharp gains near midsession on reports of mill shutdowns and forest fires in Canada. But followthrough demand was lacking and selling also developed on a continued weak cash market, they said.
"Even with mill closings and forest fires, cash is still weak," one trader said. "Having mills close because of overproduction is bearish."
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $350 per tbf, off $8 from Friday and $12 under the last midweek level.
Some activity was cited in the cash market but selling prices were under the official quote, cash sources added.
